images.alt: Known Enough brings private answers, a shared proposal, and individual approvals into one decision workflow.
images.caption: The idea in one view: private answers become a proposal people review together. Illustrative overview with fictional data.

images.alt: The current options editor lets an organizer name a decision, add topics, and review restaurant alternatives.
images.caption: Define what the group is choosing before asking what works for each person. Actual interface rendered locally with fictional data.

images.alt: A participant privately selects acceptable restaurants and a date in the What works for you form.
images.caption: People can accept several options without sharing their complete answers with the group. Actual interface rendered locally with fictional data.

images.alt: Decision chat and Private assistant provide separate conversation spaces in the current web interface.
images.caption: The conversation supports the decision rather than replacing it. Actual component with fictional local messages; this capture does not demonstrate a live model response.

images.alt: The React app uses Cognito, an API Gateway and Lambda backend, DynamoDB state, and a bounded Bedrock assistance branch.
images.caption: AI suggests, application rules validate, and people approve. This simplified architecture shows Bedrock assisting the backend without granting it approval authority.

images.alt: Private answers, optional AI assistance, explicit sharing, and separate conversations make the privacy boundaries visible.
images.caption: Privacy is expressed through specific choices: saving answers, requesting AI help, and allowing a disclosure are separate actions. Illustrative product overview.

images.alt: The actual application records Decision agreed after all fifteen test participants approve the same dinner outcome.
images.caption: The last required approval changes the result to Decision agreed. Preserved application capture from the 20 October qualification with fifteen fictional test accounts.
